content:
I forgot to include this in my main thing (that I'm replying to to continue off of) but removing soulforges is a foolish endeavor. Most characters released in arc 2 were designed around or with their soulforge passive in mind (most notably Murphy: Fauxborn who relies on her faction passive specifying "other lemurians", and Arachne who gets her Final Verdict *doubled* while it's not able to recieve most other buffs due to being a singular insulated mechanic). These characters would be completely crippled and useless without these passives intact, especially compared with other future units who will have an arc 3 passive baked into their kits the same way. This also affects arc 1 units who had complete, if outdated, kits who got new life and new use through their soulforge mechanics and became archetype-defining. To scrap Casiah's passive, one of the biggest enablers of Discard teams, would be to hinder the entire team building around them especially when such strong characters like Pontos rely almost entirely on that passive. Other characters received unique synergies like Goliath who despite having no interaction with tentacle damage received a buff that made him work well with the aforementioned iteration of Murphy. Without these passives these fan favorites will fade into obscurity and have no reason to use them going into arc 3. There is the argument that these passives will be part of the new ones to avoid nerfing them post purchase, but that would be lazy design. I have an alternative. 

Instead of replacing passives, make them additive. This keeps characters not only where they are and as strong as they are, but also allows them to become even stronger with new mechanics and new characters. Expand upon Lemurian team building, or develop the poison/counter/bleed/discard archetypes without trying to bulldoze over what was already made. Players shouldn't have to memorize multiple distinct kits for the same character.

content:
Regarding DTide a lot of people are way too focused on the introduction (and removal) of <!6!> extra pulls worth of currency which is such a meaningless change compared to the new difficulty system.
With the new recommended levels (assuming enemy level and scaling is consistent with the current version) the entire spectrum of difficulty from a1 to a5 is squished into just normal and hard modes. A major chunk of the playerbase is going to be forced to either play a way too easy mode with lacking resources or push an unfun difficulty just to get the same rewards they used to get while actually having fun (for example as a 375 player i will now need to push a difficulty HARDER than current a5 just to get the same reward i get right now at my comfortable sweetspot). The new reward system leaves everyone but 325 and 425 players at a disadvantage. 300 gets removed, 350 has no access to refined pyramids and 375 described above.
Additionally the progression between waves is also way to broad. Hard w1 seems to be easier than a4w1 yet Hard w5 is going to be worse than current a5w5. 
Gnosis use is not a good solution to this problem, but it sure is significantly better than no gnonis. It lets players bypass the wave to wave scaling (aka be able to play hard without whale supports even if w5 is now unclearable for your account). It also allows people to punch up and get refineds to actually progress their account outside of gacha. Since it doesnt count for leaderboards there is no downside to allowing it for reward collection. Please consider rolling back the rollback!
A7 as a whale playground is better than hpbloating a5.

Bonded covs are a bad idea, as they introduce even more grind to the grindiest system in the game. However cancelling them 1 day after announcement shows a lack of a clear design plan on the part of the devs.

content:
Non-endgame changes:

I like all the changes presented, and you did a really good job with the 2.5 changes to dailies and weeklies and I trust you know what you're doing <:slugcat_thumbsup:742463854277034015> 

D-Tide feedback

I like making D-Tide's floors match the rest of the game. "Madness" is easier to remember than "Alert 5".

With D-Tide at the moment the only way BIAV have to make it feel fresh is add new mobs/bosses to it or ramp the stats of the bosses. Bosses/mobs are expensive to make and nobody wants endless HP inflation like it's a Hoyoverse game because it contradicts everyone's goal of keeping all characters meta-relevant. 

To me it feels like the solution is to look at the Astral Reign ruleset and consider having additional modifiers on top of it that change seasonally, only at nightmare/madness mode, that force strategies to change. This could be done via relics. The trick is doing it without making it loads more work, so this could be refreshed each major patch (so you only need to refresh it four or five times a year).

Traphase going into maintenance mode:

The big blocker for Traphase for me is learning new decks and strategies, and anything you do there to make that easier would make me more likely to play it each month. It has a difficulty cliff at the moment, not a difficulty curve. Keeping the content the same for a while and sorting out the new player experience would encourage way more people to play it.

IMO you should consider making Traphase new character and major balance changes be tied to one patch release per major patch cycle - maybe the x.x.1 patch. This would allow it to have one big interesting drop per quarter rather than three or four smaller, harder-to-keep-up-with drops. 

Otherwise:

What matters most to me is that the game's dev team is healthy and is able to build towards a proper content buffer and a stable plan for the future of the game. I know how hard it is to work on a game where content is being finalised in the days before a patch and how chaotic it is trying to get player feedback in such environments. I also know how hard it is to not let ego get in the way when players dislike a proposed change.

The worst-case scenario for things like D-Tide is getting into an endless cycle of making Alert 5 harder and harder to the point where veterans start being unable to clear it without BIAV stepping in to buff older characters, which in turn hurts every other piece of content in the game via powercreep. You're on the right track and I wish you luck in getting this right.

EDIT:

Given the timeout I'll just stick how I'd maybe approach it at the bottom of this post:

x.x.0 patch - new story awakener, new story content, big new features, etc
x.x.1 patch - new awakener, new traphase cards and balance patch "season"
x.x.2 patch - new awakener, D-Tide ruleset update "season"

Then on to the next x.x.0 patch. So it's a healthy cadence. That would also mean players always have something to look forward to depending on what they like in Morimens - there's always a scheduled patch coming for their favourite thing soon-ish.

**D-Zone**: i frequently feel like one difficulty is too easy, but the next one is too hard, so i think we need more difficulty tiers in-between.
on top of that, the extra clear teams that would normally be the most appropriate choice could be underinvested, a choice to lower difficulty for it while still rewarding it would smooth out the progression.

higher difficulty tiers would be good as long as there's no pressure for extra rewards,
but i think it would be a better idea to add it as a reward for disabling OE/AA instead,
this would both raise the difficulty and make it easier to keep the promise of not balancing the endgame around E3.

D-Zone **revives**: i think the biggest problem with them is the impact on replays/records, i use them to learn more about the game, and revives would either promote bad playstyles if they're not hidden, or promote high spenders if they are. both options are bad for learning.

Covenant **Bonding**: it would be a good change if substats didn't exist in the first place,
i'm already burnt out from rolling substats from other games, but i think it can still be salvaged by creating a new resource/mechanic that makes it significantly easier to get perfect substats.

**Traphase**: i think the biggest problem is that it's completely different from main game, so there's too much to learn, but not enough incentive to do so. a PvE mode with better rewards and preset/reduced choice of characters would've been an easy fix.

**Affinity/Attunement**: it's still too expensive, why not just remove it from shops entirely and turn it into a high-tier reward for D-Zone or events?

content:
Posting here what I did on Reddit: Putting aside the issue of emergency gnosis, I wanted to propose a different solution to giving whales a way to compete for the dtide leaderboards rather than nightmare and madness mode. To me, massive hp inflation is more tedious than fun, and madness mode having 9x the hp of current alert 5 sounds very unfun. It will lead to more cheesy strats and less diverse gameplay. Just look at madness rail, which is almost all Clem teams, and madness pdive, which is almost all Gmurphy and Tawil teams.

In current dtide, there is an amazing variety of teams and strategies. Sure, there are common cores of teams that appear often, but it really is awesome to look at the leaderboards and see many differences between teams, wheels, and tactics. To some extent, this reflects the fact that you need multiple teams. But it also reflects the creativity that is possible at the current level of balance.

Instead of making hp sponges in nightmare and madness dtide, which will severely limit the leaderboard meta, I think a more simple, elegant solution would be to allow another extra clear. This would not affect the people who just want to do a single clear to rush for their biweekly dtide rewards. But it would allow whales to use the many characters they’ve built up over the years in new and interesting teams to strive for a 450 score, and keep an incentive for whales to pull for older characters, too. Personally, as a whale who gets 425 every dtide (and then has little to do afterwards), I would much rather try to clear another set of teams in alert 5 with wonky underused awakeners than have hp-inflated enemies that require specific, preset strategies. To me, that leans away from the strength of Morimens’s gameplay rather than towards it.

I would also add that I don’t mind some hp inflation. That’s inevitable in gacha games, and there has been reasonable hp inflation over time in dtide so far. But a jump to 9x hp seems extreme and less fun to me

The new dtide threshold is meant to give old players and whales something to grind for. To reach that level, we already had to invest a lot of silver into our characters in the first place. So why is it unreasonable for us to get some of that investment back as a reward for pushing the hardest content?

Nightmare and above is optional. Nobody needs to clear it to enjoy the game or progress normally. If someone isn't strong enough to clear it yet, that's totally fine, they can keep playing and eventually get there. But removing the reward just because newer players can't reach it right now would defeat the purpose of having an endgame difficulty in the first place. If every reward has to be immediately accessible to new players, there will eventually be nothing meaningful left for veteran players to chase. And for the one who don't want to play, it's their choice, you can't just hope for the free stuff that you not put effort to grind.

In comparison, for a new player who can't get to higher difficult yet, before the update, they get nothing; after the update, they can get something after a while. For a player that don't want to try, before and after the update they get nothing, it's the same. So the update don't even effect their silver income, why adjust them just because they won't get it either way.

I don't think new players should get less. I just don't think old players and whale should get less either. We should get what we deserve. After all the old player is the one stand with the game through up and down and the whale is the one that help keep it going.

content:
**On DTide changes:**
Raising the difficulty ceiling is inarguably a good thing, but doing so by turning every enemy into a damage sponge is an uninspired and an undesired approach that hurts some characters a lot more than the others
I would really want to believe that BIAV are capable of coming up with endgame content that is more engaging than just A5 with the HP numbers multiplied by 6

Current DTide is a cleverly designed system that helps with keeping older units relevant, and I would love for BIAV to expand on this, giving players more reasons to utilize the entirety of their roster, rather than simply adding a difficulty that will render half of the units worthless due to their inability to compete in it 

**On covenant bonding:**
Sacrificing flexibility for a handful of extra stats in a game that is supposedly all about flexible team building is a weird, clumsy and awkward system that really doesn't feel like it belongs
I struggle to think of a single good reason for it existing, almost every single character has multiple applications in multiple different teams, which require them to use a variety of covenants 

Adding a system that encourages players to ignore the other core system is a really weird direction that makes me question BIAV's vision as a whole 

**Overall feedback:**
Outside of the shop changes and the new affinity grind reason, which are okay, these announced changes feel strangely off the mark

The mode that is getting a rework is the one that needs it the least, considering Phantasmal Dive and HSR feel like an utterly irrelevant chore at the moment 
Why not rework those modes into something more fun and engaging instead? 

The fact that all this is being announced while the freshly released Lotan is riddled with unaddressed bugs and undesired voice line changes with 0 communication on that matter does not really add to my excitement and confidence either
Very much concerned about BIAV's vision for the game and their priorities

content:
D-Tide: I actually quite like the proposed changes - it adds more content and rewards for long-term players, while making it easier for less invested players to get the "current" rewards with ecogs if needed. I do wish HSR or P-dive got some of this love instead - out of the endgame modes, D-Tide was already the best. I also think it would be nice if it was expanded horizontally instead of just vertically - with the ever increasing number of awakeners, maybe time for a wave 6?
Covenants: Binding as proposed is a bit disappointing to me. I like the convenience of bound covenants, and honestly I don't mind too much having the covenant set locked from use on other awakeners, but I wish an awakener with a bonded covenant could still swap freely (or bond multiple sets). Some awakeners have multiple covenant sets to run with them and it'd be nice to be able to still use both on them.
Affinity: Proposed changes seem cool, I do think the affinity unlocks are a bit too expensive. They're cosmetics, so I don't really mind, but they're _so_ pricey it seems hard to strive for.
Shop changes: Good, no notes
Traphase: Really sad about no caraboo but hopefully the break in new content allows for a good rework and we can put everyone back in soon!
Arc 3/no soulforge: hard to say without full context, but I'm a bit worried about mechanic creep on modes? Arc 1/2 rulesets being different is already a bit hard to explain to players and keep track of, if arc 3 is sufficiently different that's just going to make it more confusing, especially when endgame modes are split between them.
